Three years of hard work, gone in an instant. This is what happened - everyone, please watch this video to the end and be vigilant to prevent this kind of thing from happening to you. Nowadays, scammers really are everywhere.

It was in March when I was browsing on my phone during my free time and came across a livestream. It was a livestream with zero followers. After I entered, they were giving away things, saying that for just one yuan, you could order a 99-yuan gift package of exquisite ceramics. I placed an order with a "let me try" mentality. Unexpectedly, it actually went through successfully. Since I spent so little, I forgot about it. A week later, I received a package. When I opened it, sure enough, it was the ceramics - there were six bowls, four plates, six pairs of chopsticks, four spoons, and those small strips. When I received this item, I was really happy, like I'd won the lottery. From then on, the nightmare began.

After bringing it home, I treasured it. On the third day, someone suddenly called me. They asked if I had received a package. I said yes. They said, "Is your address such-and-such? What did you receive? What's your number? What's your name?" I said everything was correct. At that time, I was still a bit cautious. After they told me all this information, I said yes, it's all correct. They said they were the merchant and had selected five lucky viewers out of 100 people to send another gift package - an electric pressure cooker, multifunctional, saying it sells for several hundred in stores, and they wanted to send it to me. "Let me verify this information with you." I said okay. They said because the amount was relatively large, I needed to verify that it was really me, and they would send me a verification code for me to tell them. At that time, I didn't think they could be scammers. So while on the phone, they told me not to tell anyone else and to tell them quickly. After they finished the computer operation on their end, they would ship it to me immediately. I was particularly nervous, so I told them. After I told them, in the afternoon - this happened around 10 o'clock in the morning, and then in the afternoon, I wanted to check if the slippers I bought had arrived, so I went to pick up the package.

I noticed that my text messages generally don't notify me - there's no ringtone. Then when I opened it, I suddenly saw a message displayed. At such-and-such time, over 100,000 yuan from your bank card was completely withdrawn. I was stunned. I thought it was spam, but when I looked, it was indeed sent from the bank. I panicked and didn't know what to do. I grabbed the card and rushed to our rural credit union to check. Sure enough, my husband's wages from three years of work, our family's entire income from three years, from farming - everything was gone. Only fifty cents remained in the card. I panicked then, instantly became very flustered, didn't know what to do, didn't know who to tell. So the staff said, "You'd better hurry and report this to the police." I called the police, and after they came, sure enough, all 107,000 yuan from that morning had been transferred away. They investigated and found it had been transferred to someone else's card - there was no way to recover it. At that time, there really was no solution.

I only told my family, and they couldn't accept it. The whole family blamed me, saying I acted without thinking, that I was greedy for small advantages. The pressure was enormous. In the end, my husband and I fought every day, he wanted a divorce, and I became depressed, severely depressed. I couldn't sleep all night. Although this didn't happen to me personally, it really did happen right beside us. Yesterday afternoon, a customer in the store, a woman in her 40s, not yet 50, said she couldn't sleep all night and her back hurt. I asked if something was bothering her. When she told me about this, tears streamed down her face as she spoke.

So to all the sisters in front of the screen, you must be vigilant. We must believe that pies don't fall from the sky - what falls might be a trap.; actions: type: watch, play_duration: 1, played_loop_cnt: 0, is_complete_play: False, is_fast_forward_play: False, is_backward_play: False, is_enlarge_play: False

The man manages outside affairs, the woman manages inside affairs.; asr: In Dongchi Village, there was a 25-year-old woodcutter named Jiang Liu. His parents had died early, leaving him alone in the household. Being poor, he had never been able to marry. One day, after finishing his wood cutting, he was walking by the river outside the village when he saw a young woman struggling in the water—clearly she had accidentally fallen in. "My name is Ding Xiang, I'm from the neighboring village. I was washing clothes by the river just now when I slipped and fell in. If you hadn't saved me, I might have lost my life," she said. Jiang Liu waved his hand and said, "It's nothing. You should hurry home and change into dry clothes so you don't catch cold." After chatting briefly, they each went home. About ten days later, Jiang Liu had saved up some money and hired a matchmaker to help him find a wife. Coincidentally, the woman the matchmaker introduced to him was none other than Ding Xiang, whom he had rescued. When they met, they recognized each other and felt it was truly fate. Before long, they were married. The couple had a very good relationship. Ding Xiang pointed at the empty courtyard and said to Jiang Liu, "This courtyard is too bare. In summer, there isn't even a shady spot. At my parents' home, there's a big locust tree that's especially comfortable to sit under in summer. Let's plant one too. What do you think?" Jiang Liu smiled and nodded, "Sure, if you like locust trees, let's plant one tomorrow." The next day, Ding Xiang found a small locust tree sapling. Jiang Liu took a shovel and started digging a hole in the courtyard to plant the tree. Unexpectedly, after digging for just a short while, he hit something hard—a jar. When they opened it, inside was gleaming silver! The couple carried the jar into the house and counted it—a full two hundred taels. This was roughly equivalent to twenty years of Jiang Liu's income from cutting wood. The couple was overjoyed. But a problem soon arose: who should manage all this silver? Jiang Liu said, "I'm the man, I'm the head of this household, so naturally the silver should be managed by me." Ding Xiang disagreed, "What kind of logic is that? Just because you're male? I'm afraid you'll spend it recklessly and use it all up before long. What will we do when we have children—will the whole family drink the northwest wind? It's more reliable if I keep it." Jiang Liu countered, "This silver was dug up from my courtyard. It must have been left by my ancestors, so naturally I should manage it." Ding Xiang replied, "If I hadn't said we should plant a tree, would you have dug up the silver? So I should manage it." The two argued back and forth, neither yielding. Finally, Jiang Liu said, "How about this—let's make a bet. From now on, neither of us is allowed to speak. Whoever speaks first loses. The winner will be the head of the household and manage the silver. How about it?" Ding Xiang had a stubborn temperament and thought this was a good idea, so she said, "Fine, who's afraid of who?" The two really didn't say a word. Their neighbor, Aunt Zhao, found it strange that she hadn't heard the young couple make any sound these past few days, so she went to Jiang Liu's house and asked, "Liu, why haven't I heard you speak these past few days? Is your throat bad?" Jiang Liu just waved his hand and pointed at his mouth, as if to say his throat was uncomfortable. Aunt Zhao didn't understand, so she asked Ding Xiang, "What's wrong with you two? Did you eat something wrong and lose your voices?" Ding Xiang also just waved her hand without speaking. Seeing their expressions, Aunt Zhao guessed they might be having a quarrel, so she kindly advised, "You two, if there's a problem, talk it out. Each give a little—harmony in the family brings success in everything." Seeing that neither would speak, Aunt Zhao had no choice but to leave. A few days later, Ding Xiang's 15-year-old brother, Ding Long, came to visit. As soon as he entered, he called out, "Sister! Brother-in-law!" Jiang Liu and Ding Xiang didn't speak, just smiled at him. Ding Long found it strange and kept staring at them. Near noon, Ding Xiang and Jiang Liu were cooking in the kitchen. Jiang Liu thought that since Ding Long rarely visited, he should treat him well. So he picked up a cleaver, held it in front of his neck, and pointed at Ding Long outside, gesturing to his wife. He meant to say he would go buy a big pig's head to treat his brother-in-law. Unfortunately, this gesture was seen by Ding Long, who was terrified, thinking his brother-in-law was going to use the knife to cut off his head. type: Video Browsing; ocr: The man is critically ill and his life hangs in the balance, yet he's still thinking of his unsuspecting wife. His life is about to enter its final countdown, and at this moment, Old Xia is still drinking with the cadres for Yang Bai's work. However, instead of seeing Ziheng, he unexpectedly came across his own medical report. Old Xia, helpless, can only write his inner pain in his diary. As long as he adjusts his mindset and lets go of his burdens, he will surely overcome the illness. To verify whether his father has liver cancer, because there is a top oncology expert in Bohai - in reality, this is all just a carrot that Ziheng dangled to distract him. His heart falls into immense struggle.; asr: The father was cooking when he suddenly fainted and collapsed. His two children and wife rushed over to check on him. Daughter Xiao Bai strongly insisted on taking him to the hospital immediately. But Old Xia, not wanting to trouble his family, lied and claimed he just hadn't slept well. However, he never imagined that his life was about to enter its final countdown. Early yesterday morning, Old Xia endured the pain to polish shoes for his family, and carefully helped Yang Bai with hers. Watching her father humble himself to serve her mother, Xiao Bai burned with anger inside, because she knew her mother didn't love her father at all. So she begged her mother to accompany father to see a doctor, but Yang Bai was obsessed with opera all day long and didn't care about her husband's condition at all. In the end, Old Xia went to the hospital alone for examination. After the examination, Da Peng told Uncle Xia to go home first and would notify him immediately when there was news. A few hours later, Da Peng took the CT scan to find his father. "Late-stage liver cancer? You must be joking. This is nothing. Who took this?" Zi Heng was stunned on the spot. He picked up the CT scan and looked at it again. He couldn't believe it was true, so he notified all the authoritative experts in the hospital. The experts all shook their heads - there was no treatment value left. Meanwhile, Xiao Bai was asking Da Peng about her father's condition. Da Peng, afraid they would worry, didn't reveal the truth. Zi Heng looked at Old Xia's CT scan, both anxious and helpless, but for Yang Bai's sake, he had to find a way to save Old Xia. At this time, Old Xia was still drinking with officials for Yang Bai's work. However, while drinking... Zi Heng forcibly required Old Xia to be hospitalized, but Old Xia insisted on not staying to take care of Yang Bai, who never cooked. As they were talking, Xiao Bai rushed over. Learning that father vomited blood from drinking, Xiao Bai instantly knew father had drunk so much for mother's sake again, which added more resentment to Xiao Bai's existing hatred toward her mother. Old Xia's condition was urgent. Zi Heng believed Xiao Bai had grown up and had the right to know the truth, so he told her everything about Old Xia's condition. Yang Bai instantly broke down. She didn't believe father could have this disease, and even suspected Zhou Zi Heng deliberately diagnosed liver cancer to be with mother, wanting to scare Old Xia to death. Unable to accept reality, Xiao Bai sadly rushed out. She so hoped this wasn't true. Father's whole life, he worked tirelessly for his family without complaint, yet ended up with such a fate. At this time, the unaware Old Xia came to find Zi Heng to discuss discharge, but instead of seeing Zi Heng, he accidentally saw his own examination report - late stage. Learning of his condition, Old Xia's legs went weak and he collapsed to the ground. This sudden change left Old Xia in despair. Even at this point, to take care of Yang Bai, he still secretly ran out of the hospital and specially made his wife's favorite chicken stewed with mushrooms. Yang Bai had lost her former glory. Now the troupe was dominated by young people. Although she had no place in the troupe, she still regarded opera as the most important career in her life. Old Xia could only helplessly write his inner pain in his diary. He was unwilling and didn't want to die so early. He still wanted to write another play for his wife to fulfill Yang Bai's long-cherished wish. At this time, Yang Bai came home. Old Xia endured the pain and faced his wife with a smile as usual. Unexpectedly, Zhou Zi Heng also came to their home. He came for Old Xia's illness, hoping Old Xia would return to the hospital for treatment immediately. Old Xia worried Yang Bai would learn of his condition, so he took Zi Heng outside. Zi Heng comforted Old Xia that among the tumor patients he had cured, some lived five years, some ten years, and some twenty years. As long as he adjusted his mindset and let go of his burden, he could definitely overcome the disease. But Old Xia wasn't actually afraid of death; he just wanted to do more things for Yang Bai before dying

But she picked up all the eggs and meat from her mother's bowl and put them into her own, then ignored her mother beside her and began eating heartily. Even the restaurant owner couldn't stand watching. Just as he was about to scold the girl for being inconsiderate, suddenly a bundle of cash fell from the girl's body. This immediately sparked an inexplicable anger in the owner, who questioned why the girl, clearly having money, would pretend to be pitiful in front of him to get free noodles. The girl hastily explained that this was money for her mother's surgery tomorrow and couldn't be used. After her mother's surgery tomorrow, she would definitely collect bottles to pay the owner back. But the owner clearly didn't believe the girl's words. If the girl's mother was having surgery tomorrow, why was she only concerned with eating and drinking herself, ignoring her mother, and even taking all the meat from her mother's bowl? Someone so selfish like her. But the girl's next words plunged him into deep self-reproach: "If I don't eat my fill, I'm afraid I won't have the strength to donate a kidney to my mother tomorrow. My mother only has one kidney left and will die tomorrow. The doctor can't find a suitable kidney source, and I can't afford it. I can only use my own kidney to save my mother." To make the owner believe her words, the girl took out a voluntary kidney donation agreement and removed the prayer beads her mother gave her, pressing them into the owner's hand, claiming this was the only valuable thing her mother gave her. She would leave it with the owner as collateral and redeem it later when she earned money. She said she could eat less in the future and promised to quickly make up the remaining noodle money. Only then did the owner realize he had misunderstood the girl, and was moved by her filial devotion. So he told the girl she could eat and drink at his place anytime without charge. Qiu Ling, in order to fulfill their happiness, decided to be siblings with Zhao Shijun from then on, but on the surface they still had to address each other as husband and wife, because her father-in-law still controlled the water source of Shahe Town. Once he knew his daughter was sleeping alone, he would surely cut off the water supply to the entire town. The maid couldn't bear to see Miss Qiuling wronging herself like this and actually told Master Wan about it. Xiuzhu didn't lie. I have been letting Qiuling down all along. We have never had marital relations. Zhao Shijun didn't evade responsibility and frankly admitted he and Qiuling had never been intimate as husband and wife. In a rage, Wan Daquan pulled out his pistol and aimed it at Zhao Shijun's head, wanting to vent this anger for his daughter, but unexpectedly Qiu Ling blocked Shijun, claiming that if Father shoots today, he should kill her first. Wan Daquan looked at this disappointing daughter with great frustration. Zhao Shijun couldn't bear to let Qiuling take the blame and wanted to confess everything, but Qiuling reminded him in time that impulse is the devil. Please punish us for being absent for so long. Suddenly collapsing, after Zhao Shijun heard Qiuling's advice, he indeed became more impulsive, immediately pointing his father-in-law's gun at his own heart. He would take responsibility for his own actions alone, only asking his father-in-law not to implicate the common people of Shahe Town. But just before leaving, Wan Daquan issued a warning to Zhao Shijun: I want her to be your real wife. This steward is stealing my celebration. Zhao Shijun had always felt he wronged Qiuling, but if they really became husband and wife, his heart suddenly ached, thinking about how he couldn't acknowledge his daughter. Xinzi was still suffering outside. Zhao Shijun made up his mind. I will take you and Xiuyun together. Would you go die for me? I've heard enough of others condemning you. Our whole family has only one choice: live together, die together. Zhao Shijun's decision greatly comforted Xinci. She hadn't loved the wrong person after all and decisively agreed to go with him to face Baogong Temple together. Even if they died, the family of three would die together. Unexpectedly, when the two were reliving their happiness, they were discovered by Brother Li. All along, Xinci refused to reveal who the child's father was. Everyone thought that man was a heartless scoundrel who abandoned Xinci. Now seeing this man, Brother Li immediately wanted to expose the true face of the lucky scoundrel, but before he could get close, he was knocked unconscious by the scoundrel. Although Zhao Shijun's identity wasn't exposed, unless you kill me. Hmph, I said your mother didn't hear you went. Just watching Brother Li's hostility toward the lucky scoundrel made Xinci terrified. To protect Zhao Shijun, she decided to have Brother Li take her away from here. Xinci's request was exactly what Brother Li wanted, so the two agreed to secretly set off after Sister-in-law fell asleep, but before they left, they learned from Liang Yongchang that Zhao Shijun had been ambushed and beaten half to death. Liang Yongchang had always resented Xinci for breaking off their engagement and hated Zhao Shijun even more for taking Xinci. Finally finding an opportunity for revenge, this is mine. Don't let a family of three be separated. Mm, stealing my woman, stealing my woman, hehe. Afterward, Liang Yongchang deliberately found Xinci and lied that Zhao Shijun had been beaten, also hinting it was Brother Li who did it. Because Brother Li had previously been full of hostility toward the scoundrel father, Xinci believed it and was both anxious and afraid. type: Video Browsing; caption: The man clearly knew the porridge brought by the maid was poisoned, yet he still ate it in big gulps without hesitation #MangoTVPromotionPlan #FastTalkDramaReview #LoveBlossoms; ocr: Qixiu was binge-watching a series. With conflicted and complicated feelings, still lying unconscious in the hospital.; asr: The man clearly knew the porridge sent by the maid was poisoned, yet he acted as if nothing was wrong and ate it in large mouthfuls. Soon the bowl of porridge was finished. He smiled faintly, quietly waiting for death to arrive. It wasn't until Zhu Daofeng's hand dropped limply that Youlan's tears finally burst forth. She had finally taken revenge on this villain who had violated her sister, but she felt no satisfaction from her revenge. Instead, her heart ached as if being torn apart. At some point during the process of seeking revenge, she had quietly fallen in love with this man. Heartbroken, Youlan ran all the way to Wutong Lane in one breath. In a trance, her deceased sister appeared before her, praising her for doing well: "You finally brought him to see me. You truly are my good sister. Remember, don't miss me too much." "I don't want him to die!" In the end, her attachment to Zhu Daofeng overcame her hatred. Youlan panicked and ran to seek help from Zhu Daofeng's friend. "He's dying, what should I do?" "What happened to Daofeng? What's going on?" She couldn't bring herself to say that she had poisoned Zhu Daofeng, and could only flee in panic. Carrying conflicting and complicated feelings, Youlan chose to drown herself in the river to seek release. Fortunately, Qingchuan happened to pass by and pulled her back from death's grasp. Meanwhile, Zhu Daofeng was sent to the hospital. Although his life was saved, he remained unconscious. Youlan, who was his personal maid, was nowhere to be found. Master Zhu was certain his son's condition was connected to Youlan and notified the police to arrest her. On the other side, Youlan, who had been unconscious for several days, finally woke up. She told Qingchuan the whole truth about poisoning Zhu Daofeng without reservation. But as Zhu Daofeng's friend, Qingchuan refused to believe that Zhu Daofeng, who was like a perfect gentleman, could do such beastly things. Soon Master Zhu found Youlan hiding at Qingchuan's house through a private detective. "You finally appeared. Don't tell me you've forgotten those three words 'Gu Maiqing.'" Looking at Youlan before him, Master Zhu finally remembered she was the younger daughter of his old friend Gu. Youlan angrily accused him of allowing his son to assault her sister, causing her father to die seeking revenge. She had wanted to live peacefully with her mother, but after her mother became mentally ill, her whereabouts remained unknown to this day. It turned out that Master Zhu, out of guilt, had taken it upon himself to bring her mother to England for treatment. He had intended for the butler to bring Youlan on the next ship to England to reunite with them. Unexpectedly, after Youlan was accidentally bitten by a dog, she hid herself, so the butler could never find her. Thus, through a series of mishaps, Youlan was separated from her mother for many years. What was even more unexpected was that after all her scheming to get close to Zhu Daofeng to avenge her sister, she discovered she had targeted the wrong person. It turned out that on the day of the incident, Zhu Daofeng was abroad. The ruby ring was a coming-of-age gift Master Zhu had given to both his sons; each brother had one. The one who hurt her sister was someone else. Hearing this, Youlan felt thunderstruck. She never imagined her revenge would turn out to be so absurdly laughable. Devastated, she returned to the Qin household and cried uncontrollably in Mother Qin's arms. He was still lying unconscious in the hospital. Upon hearing this, Youlan immediately wanted to rush to the hospital to see him, but at the hospital she was stopped by Daofeng's friends. Facing this woman who had poisoned their friend, no one gave her a kind look. "Lijun is in the room with him. If you think you can face Lijun openly and have no guilt toward her, then go ahead." Without the courage to face Zhuang Bijun, Youlan could only leave dejectedly. Qingchuan, who arrived later, explained the whole story to everyone. To help Daofeng wake up sooner, the friends finally decided to arrange for Youlan to visit him in the ward. The next day, Zhuang Bijun was coaxed and tricked out of the ward, and Youlan took the opportunity to come to Daofeng's side. She lay on Daofeng crying her heart out. Now she prayed to heaven to let her beloved wake up quickly. Several minutes quickly passed. Before leaving, Youlan leaned close to Daofeng's ear and sighed. Reluctantly, Youlan left the ward, but just as she stepped out the door, she came face to face with Zhuang Bijun. Just when everyone thought the two women were about to have a confrontation, unexpectedly the next second— "I love you."; action

A woman schemes her way into marrying into a wealthy family, but on their wedding night, her husband would rather share a bed with a dancer than step foot in the bridal chamber. It turns out the groom doesn't love her and didn't even attend the wedding ceremony.

Yindi wore a pure white wedding dress, filled with joy, fantasizing about the comfortable life of being the young mistress. Commander Cao and his wife were very satisfied with their personally selected daughter-in-law, but the Third Concubine, who constantly opposed the First Wife, deliberately spilled the tea. "You didn't hold the tea properly yourself, why blame her? My belly was affected by her singing." But she never imagined that on her wedding night, she would sleep alone in an empty room.

Her husband paid her no attention at all. Today, however, his attitude changed 180 degrees - he suddenly embraced Yindi from behind, wanting to consummate the marriage. Cao Rui didn't feel he owed Yindi anything - she was his wife, serving him was her duty. But being someone's substitute made Yindi feel disgusted.

It turned out her sister Yinxiu had come to the Cao household as a maid, constantly appearing before Cao Rui. Cao Rui never looked at Yindi properly. Yindi grew increasingly dissatisfied with Yinxiu. Remembering that her sister had brought the sobering soup last night, Yindi became suspicious.

Uncle Li put on the new cloth shoes sent by his family.; asr: The old saying goes that the forty-nine days after a person passes away are counted from the day of death, with every seven days marking one "seven," totaling seven sevens. Don't underestimate these seven weeks—in the eyes of the older generation, this is the journey the departed soul must undergo through the underworld. Today, let me tell you about the significance of these seven stages. Just consider it a story passed down from our elders. The first seven days are called "Tou Qi." When Old Man Li had just passed, his soul was still wandering around the courtyard. He heard his son crying, saying he hadn't bought him his favorite sugar cake. Anxious and pacing, his family quickly laid out his favorite snacks and burned some paper money. Only then did Old Man Li set off on his journey, at least not going hungry. The second seven was the most precarious—underworld guards dragging iron chains came clanking to fetch him. With empty pockets, Old Man Li was pushed forward by the two guards. The gold ingots his son burned at home suddenly blazed up, transforming into gleaming gold coins that fell into his hands. Only then did the guards release him. The third seven required crossing Evil Dog Ridge, where masses of wild dogs with glowing green eyes lunged to bite. Fortunately, his family had placed meat buns at the crossing. Old Man Li grabbed the buns and threw them into the pack of dogs. As the wild dogs fought over them, he scrambled through, his pant legs torn to shreds. The fourth seven was the Gate of Ghosts. Two black doors like a giant beast's mouth, with ghost guards standing at the entrance demanding a toll. His family twisted sesame stalks and burned them, crackling and transforming into golden and silver light that enveloped Old Man Li. The ghost guards nodded, and the doors opened a crack. He quickly slipped through. The fifth seven reached the Cockcrow Pass. Old Man Li quietly returned home in the middle of the night to find the main door wide open. In the ashes on the stove, there were indeed several small footprints. Just as he was about to reach out and touch his grandson's face, the rooster crowed at the fifth watch, and his whole body trembled. He had no choice but to retreat outside—one moment slower and he would have been trapped in the house by the morning light. On the sixth seven, Old Man Li climbed the Homesickness Terrace, but before him was only fog and he could see nothing. Not until the paper money burned by his family floated up did the mist gradually clear. He saw corn drying in the courtyard and his little grandson chasing butterflies. Just as tears were about to well up, he heard crows cawing—urging him to continue his journey. On the seventh seven, at the Bridge of No Return, Lady Meng held out a bowl of soup. Old Man Li put on the new cloth shoes his family had burned for him, took the bowl, and drank it all in one gulp. Past memories scattered like smoke blown by the wind. He lifted his foot and stepped onto the bridge. On the other side was bright light—it was time to go to the next life.; actions: type: watch, play_duration: 2, played_loop_cnt: 0, is_complete_play: False, is_fast_forward_play: False, is_backward_play: False, is_enlarge_play: False

On the wedding day, when he saw the groom's appearance, he suddenly vomited uncontrollably. The groom was very worried and rushed forward to diagnose her, but the result shocked him. Why was there a life? It turned out the woman was named Shi Aoshuang. Once when she went up the mountain to gather firewood, she encountered a group of local ruffians. Just as they were about to succeed, a handsome man descended from the sky and protected Aoshuang behind him. Seeing the woman about to slip away, and unable to defeat this man, the thugs in anger shot a poisoned cold arrow at her. The man quickly moved Aoshuang and brought her to a small house to treat her wounds. Unexpectedly, the sky suddenly filled with thunder and lightning, and heavy rain poured down. The man was shivering from the cold, and Aoshuang, to repay his life-saving grace, removed her clothes to warm the man. Unexpectedly, the man waking from his daze, looking at the beautiful Aoshuang before him, couldn't control himself and something happened between them. But when the man woke again the next day, he didn't remember last night's events. Seeing this, Aoshuang no longer mentioned what happened. Little did she know the man before her was actually Emperor Kangxi traveling in disguise. A few days later, Manager Qu brought people and found this place. Seeing such grand circumstances before her, Aoshuang knew this man must be of great wealth and status, and she was not worthy of him. So Aoshuang resolutely bid them farewell and left alone. Later, through her parents' arrangement, Aoshuang was forced to marry the neighboring young master Lin Youqing. "With my physical condition, I cannot have children anymore. Alas, this time I really made a mistake." Looking at the gentle and kind Lin Youqing, Aoshuang's heart was filled with mixed feelings. However, her pregnancy was soon discovered by her mother-in-law, who scolded that not only was her son cuckolded, but he also became a backup. Mother Lin wanted Youqing to divorce Aoshuang, but Youqing insisted on taking responsibility for Aoshuang. Mother Lin was furious and hurried to consult Father Lin. Unexpectedly, Father Lin was very happy upon learning his daughter-in-law was pregnant and comforted Mother Lin to accept this child. Their son's body couldn't produce children; perhaps this was heaven taking pity on them so the Lin family wouldn't end without descendants. Ten months later, Aoshuang successfully gave birth to a baby boy. [The family] loved him like their own son, and the family of three lived an extremely happy life. However, happy days are always short-lived. Youqing's health deteriorated. That night he went out again to buy candied hawthorn for Long'er. Unexpectedly, on the return journey, heavy rain suddenly poured down, which undoubtedly made Youqing's condition worse. When the family brought the unconscious Youqing home, the doctor issued a critical condition notice. Knowing his days were numbered, Youqing instructed Long'er to shoulder the responsibility of being a man and take good care of Aoshuang and the Lin parents in his place. He then urged Aoshuang not to remain a widow after his death, but Aoshuang disagreed, saying she would always be his person and would definitely raise Long'er and make the Lin family prosper. Unexpectedly, after Youqing's death, Uncle Lin Youfu, in order to seize the Lin family property, secretly murdered the Lin elders and framed Aoshuang. This scene happened to be seen by Long'er who had secretly followed. Afterward, Lin Youfu filed a lawsuit against Aoshuang at the yamen to monopolize the family property, not only accusing her of murdering her parents-in-law but also exposing that she was unchaste and pregnant before marriage.

type: Video Browsing; ocr: I am Chu Ruixue. In everyone's impression, I've always been a tough, iron-willed woman. But today, the company gave me a task—to talk about the first half of my life. Where should I start with the theater of my life? I always feel that talking about my childhood hardships and entrepreneurial journey might seem a bit affected. Facing a hundred million fans, I think it's necessary to open my heart and talk about my past. This video might be a bit long; I hope you have the patience to watch it through.

I come from an ordinary family in Changchun. Other people's childhood memories are of playing and carefree days, but my memories are mostly of the smell of disinfectant in hospitals and the smell of blood-and-urine-stained sheets. So my childhood was spent growing up amid the crying in hospital corridors and anxious fear. In third grade, my mother was diagnosed with aplastic anemia, which was incurable at that time. From that moment on, my childhood happiness ended. My life became a two-point line between school and hospital. After school, I'd rush to the hospital to take care of my mother's every need, sleeping on a hospital bed every day. I remember very clearly—it was those old wooden benches. One bench, two benches, three benches—my head resting on one, my waist on another, and finally my legs dangling there. On this bed made of three benches, I stayed for three months at a time. Everyone in the family could only use money to race against death. The most profound truth I learned in the hospital was: if you have money, you can get blood transfusions—over a thousand yuan a day. With that blood transfusion, you can live one more day. If your family can't give you that money and they pull out the tube tomorrow, you might never see them again. So from a young age, I was different from others in one way—I loved money too much. Money saves lives. I witnessed too many separations by death in the hospital. The girl in the next bed was not even thirty, so optimistic. I thought with her optimism, she'd definitely make it. When I'm discharged, I'll go drinking with you. I also knew my mother had many emotions bottled up inside. I could only smile and encourage her to hold on a bit longer—when I grow up, I'll be able to earn lots of money. In the most difficult and helpless times, I even thought about selling myself to some family as a laborer. Could I exchange that for the money for my mother's bone marrow transplant? As long as they'd give me money, as long as it could save my mother's life, I'd give up ten years of my life, as long as my mother could get better.

On a snowy night in 2008, I'll never forget that scene—it was also the first wish I made in my life. Northeast China is really cold, and it's hard to hail a cab. Moreover, in Changchun, the streets are full of second-hand Jettas. After accompanying my mother for a blood transfusion—because transfused blood is someone else's blood, sometimes the body has a strong reaction. Because it's cold, coming from the blood bank, and it's not your own, sometimes my mother would shiver all over, unbearably cold. In the wind and snow of Northeast China, the two of us waited for two or three hours, all for that five-yuan fare, in front of a second-hand Jetta. Among so many cars, why didn't I have even one? I hugged my mother tightly—I wanted to buy a second-hand Jetta. This was my first dream in life. Was the wish fulfilled? You definitely want to know, right? In the years after that, I bought my first car in life, and I also bought a 180-square-meter house. So I always say: people still need to have dreams—what if you don't just achieve them, but surpass them? Now I can afford many cars.

For several years, my dream was that second-hand Jetta. The medical examination report came out—Dad was sick too. I asked him why he didn't go to the hospital, why he didn't treat his illness. I was especially angry. He said to me lightly, "If I go to the hospital too, there'll be no one to earn money for your mother's treatment." I knew I had to become very strong. In the future, I not only had to earn money for my mother's treatment, but I also had to be able to afford treatment for my father at any time. I often made a budget—if I wanted to keep my mother alive, how much money did I need to earn? I sang at a barbecue restaurant in Changchun. Next to me was a guitar player, on the right was a keyboard player, and I was in the middle as the face of the group. I started earning 60 yuan, which meant 1,800 yuan a month. But compared to my mother's blood transfusion costing over 1,000 yuan each time, four times a month, this amount was far from enough. I started a side business at home—opening an online store. I could earn about 30 yuan a day, adding another 1,000 yuan of monthly income. So I had about 3,000 yuan in monthly income, but it still wasn't nearly enough. Later, I established my own 10 Crown-level Taobao stores, so I'm also a very experienced women's clothing store owner. Ma

type: Video Browsing; ocr: Another mom worked herself to death, can't hold it in anymore, so angry. Saying she gets up at 4:30 in the morning to cook, buying 10 yuan worth of breakfast would be enough to eat, can the dirt really kill someone? I suddenly realized, if you can't afford expensive takeout, he'll remarry right after.; asr: Did you hear? A 38-year-old mom in Hangzhou worked herself to death. When I heard about this, I got so angry I couldn't hold it in - I just came out here, my temper got the best of me. I really want to pull her out of that coffin and slap some sense into her. This is infuriating! How could she work herself to death? How did she actually die from exhaustion? They say she had two kids. Tutoring the kids with homework, doing housework, cleaning the house, cooking - only sleeping five hours a day, and she died from exhaustion. Getting up at 4:30 in the morning to cook - what are you cooking? Are you preparing an imperial feast? Are you serving the emperor? Getting up at 4:30! If you're so exhausted, can't you get up later? You're in a big city and you work yourself to death? Aren't there plenty of places selling breakfast in the county? Steamed buns, fried dough sticks and such. Ten yuan worth of breakfast is enough to eat - do you really need to get up that early? Right? And they say after tutoring the kids with homework, she'd clean up and wouldn't go to bed until 1 AM. My god, what kind of house are you cleaning so thoroughly? Will a dirty house kill someone? Can dirt kill you? But exhaustion CAN kill you! Oh my god, she has a husband, in-laws - but can't count on them. If you can't count on others, change yourself! I used to be foolish like her. After the kids went to bed, I'd clean, do housework, keep at it, cook for them. In the end I was exhausted down to 90 pounds. Then I suddenly woke up. If you can't change others, you have to change yourself. If the house is dirty, let it be dirty. Whoever doesn't like it can clean it themselves. If you don't clean, then shut your mouth. This is how dirty I am. I'll do whatever makes me comfortable. Too lazy to cook? Order takeout. Can't afford expensive stuff? Buy instant noodles and cook them. I give myself a break, right? How could she die from exhaustion? Oh my, dying from exhaustion in a big city. Sometimes pitiful people have their hateful aspects. You don't even cherish yourself - who else will cherish you? The moment you die, they'll remarry right away. Sisters, learn from me. Look at me, disheveled all day - I just don't bother. Let others think what they want. As long as I'm comfortable, that's enough, right? Trying to change others is crazy. Being able to change yourself makes you divine. I used to be so neat and tidy. Now I'm just a bit dirty, so what? As long as I'm not exhausted, that's fine. Live however is comfortable, right, sisters? Life is just a few decades - live comfortably, love yourself. Take care of yourselves, you guys, hahaha.; actions: type: watch, play_duration: 143, played_loop_cnt: 0, is_complete_play: True, is_fast_forward_play: True, is_backward_play: True, is_enlarge_play: False

type: Video Browsing; caption: Mother teaches daughter not to stay out overnight; ocr: A mother educates her daughter: "Girls cannot spend the night out. Why not? Because there are many uncertain factors for girls outside. Her parents aren't home today, and she's waiting for me. Come here, let me tell you, staying overnight at your classmate's house, do you hear me? How long have we been playing? I'll call you to report as soon as I arrive. Come back here and stop. If I let you go today, it would harm you, and I would be failing as a mother. Tongtong, let me tell you a real case. After you hear this case, then decide whether to go or not. Three years ago, an 18-year-old girl was invited by her so-called best friend to stay at her house. When leaving, she told her mother very clearly that it would be just the two of them, her friend's parents weren't home, and her friend was scared to be alone and wanted her company. Her parents initially objected, but the girl insisted on going, so her parents finally agreed. Two girls staying together should have been fine, but you can't see into people's hearts. After this girl arrived at her classmate's house, the classmate brought out alcohol and food, saying since her parents weren't home, they should have some drinks. The two girls started drinking. While drinking, her classmate called over more than ten boys. After drinking too much, this girl lost consciousness. When she woke up the next morning, she found herself in her classmate's bed, and her life was ruined. Although the case was reported later, you know what happened. It turned out her so-called best friend owed a lot of money to people outside, and those people were the girl's creditors. Forced into a corner, she lured her classmate to her home and used this girl to pay off her debts. Although the case was solved and the bad people were punished, this girl's life was destroyed. Everyone thought he would live happily under his sisters' protection. Unexpectedly, eighteen years later, to escape arranged marriages, the young man left the family and became a ride-share driver. One day, when the young man didn't know how to compensate a female passenger for dirtying her 20,000-yuan item, two sisters who couldn't stand watching finally appeared - the president of Wanguo Commerce Association and the female CEO of Galaxy Group, Ye Qilin. type: Video Browsing; caption: #WatchingShowsTogether; ocr: Good drama recommendation. Are you getting married today? Not getting in the bridal sedan chair, she must have gotten lost. You're asking for it, just watch how I deal with you.; asr: Here is the English translation:

A man nearly fifty years old, preparing to marry for the first time, had bought a string of firecrackers, but unexpectedly they were set off by this fool in front of him. I only bought one string, planning to set them off when the bride arrived. You've gone crazy now, what will you do when the bride comes? Just as the man was blaming the fool, the matchmaker brought him more bad news. The bride was demanding additional betrothal gifts at the last minute. How could this happen? On his wedding day, where was he supposed to come up with another 100 yuan? Because Tieniu's living conditions were truly terrible, the bride was unwilling to marry into this place, so she came up with this plan to increase the betrothal money, hoping Tieniu would back out. Just when Tieniu didn't know what to do, his nephew Feng Cheng suddenly arrived from Beijing. "Uncle, you're getting married today?" Seeing his uncle getting married, Feng Cheng was very happy. He had arrived just in time for the wedding celebration. But the next second, Tieniu told Feng Cheng that there might not be any celebration after all. "What do you want me to do? I'm not the one demanding more money." Then the matchmaker turned her gaze toward Feng Cheng. With the matchmaker's reminder, Tieniu suddenly had an idea and pulled his nephew into the house with a smile. "This isn't a good woman." "What are you saying? She's your aunt." "Do you have the 100 yuan?" Feng Cheng told his uncle this wasn't about money - suddenly changing terms and demanding more money before the wedding made him feel this aunt was no good. But his uncle didn't see it that way, because he knew he lived in the desolate Saihanba, where conditions were harsh with constant wind and sand, and no one would choose to marry into such a place. Now that he finally had this chance, how could Tieniu let it slip away? To get Feng Cheng to give him money, he played the family card, saying he was his mother's only brother. If Feng Cheng's mother knew about this, she definitely wouldn't let her brother remain a bachelor for life. Unable to resist his uncle's pressure, Feng Cheng reluctantly took out 100 yuan. However, the matchmaker didn't leave after getting the money. Instead, she made a new demand. "You've prepared the sedan chair, right?" "Yes." "What about musicians? Singing and playing instruments? The girl specifically requested this. She didn't want to marry into Saihanba in the first place. She said without musicians and a sedan chair, she won't come." Tieniu was about to break down. Just as he was about to fetch his new bride, where could he find musicians now? Just when Tieniu was at a loss, Feng Cheng suddenly told his uncle he knew the harmonica and could play any tune. "Oh, you're a lifesaver! You came back to rescue your uncle!" So Tieniu prepared everything and finally brought the bride from her family home. But after walking for a long time, there wasn't even a tree's shadow around, just yellow sand everywhere. The bride felt like she was being sold off. "How much longer?" "About another hour and we'll be there. If you're tired, you can sleep for a bit." "No, that won't do. The bride can't sleep until she enters the bridal chamber, and then she has to sleep with the groom." Just as everyone was immersed in the happy atmosphere, the man carrying the sedan suddenly saw a sandstorm in the distance. "Tieniu! A dust devil is coming!" The sandstorm spared no one. Feng Cheng shouted for everyone to lie down on the spot, but the bride in the sedan didn't know what was happening and was blown away, sedan and all. After the sandstorm passed, everyone emerged from the sand piles, but only the bride was nowhere to be found. "My wife is named Wu Gaihua. She's never been to the plateau before, so she must be lost. Please, everyone, help me find my wife!" While everyone was busy searching for the bride, Tieniu's nephew Feng Cheng quietly arrived at the bride's family home. As a college graduate, he clearly understood that this sandstorm wasn't strong enough to blow someone away - only the harsh environment could scare someone into running. Sure enough, the woman soon came out of the house. Feng Cheng told the woman that since she had already registered her marriage with his uncle, she should go to Saihanba and live properly with him, not run back to her parents' home using the sandstorm as an excuse. "I heard the plateau was harsh, but I didn't realize it. We walked for two hours without seeing a single tree, just sand everywhere, and such strong winds. I won't marry him. I want a divorce." The woman's attitude was firm - there was no way to live in such conditions on Saihanba. Hearing the woman wanted a divorce, her family members ran out to persua

On their wedding night, Nurhaci eagerly anticipated lifting the red veil, only to be startled by the person before him. "I am Donggo's younger sister. My name is Meimei. I was supposed to marry Donggo. What are you doing here?" Upon learning he had been deceived, Nurhaci flew into a rage like a wild beast, dragging Menggu outside. Hearing the commotion, a maid rushed out to intervene, but with nowhere to vent his fury, he struck her backhanded, leaving her mouth bloody. At this critical moment, the maid cried out loudly for Jin Taiji to save them. Fortunately, Jin Taiji arrived in time; otherwise, the consequences would have been unthinkable. However, his next words only further enraged Nurhaci, like adding fuel to fire. "I promised my sister would marry you, so this sister must be Donggo." "You conspired together to deceive me!" Šurhaci explained with a grieved expression that he knew nothing about it. On the journey back to Jianzhou, he was still grieving over losing his beloved. But Nurhaci remained furious, refusing to listen to any explanation. As a leader, his dignity had been trampled upon. He immediately rushed outside and ordered guards to quickly mobilize troops. Even if it meant going to war with Yehe in the rain, he would bring Donggo back. "You're crazy! If you do this to Heli..." "Who dares disobey my orders!" Jin Taiji showed no weakness, immediately drawing his long sword and pointing it at Nurhaci. "If you dare send Menggu back, it would be the greatest humiliation to Yehe. I would rather die standing than endure this disgrace." As both sides remained deadlocked, Šurhaci quickly stepped forward, blocking his brother and urging him not to act rashly and to consider the consequences of blindly deploying troops. At this point, Nurhaci had completely lost his reason. He ordered archers to aim at Jin Taiji and the others. "If you harm us five, my elder brother will immediately send Yehe cavalry to flatten Jianzhou. I'll say it again: my Yehe cavalry will flatten your Jianzhou." Just as he was about to cut his own throat, Nurhaci rushed forward and grabbed the sharp blade, letting blood flow freely while his gaze remained burning and unwavering. type: Video Browsing; caption: Hello Uncle and Auntie, I'm Liang Shuang #PositiveEnergy #RecordingLife #DailyLife; ocr: May everything go as you wish. From being abandoned to being illuminated. I am Xiao Shuang. May all things turn out auspicious. May everything go as you wish, Happy New Year. I left because my family was too poor. I remember what my father said to me before he passed away. The look in her eyes at that moment. There are still people in this world who ask for nothing in return. But rather, it's the moment when two sincere hearts illuminate each other.; asr: Hello uncles and aunties, I'm Xiao Shuang. I've never had a complete family to rely on since I was little. People in the village said that when I was too young to remember, my mother left because the family was too poor. My father raised me all by himself. Although he didn't talk much, he was an honest man, but when I was 16 years old, he never came back up after saving a drowning child. From that moment on, I was truly alone. So when my mother-in-law came and said she would raise me like her own daughter, I had hope in my heart. I so desperately wanted to have a family. After I married into the family, I worked desperately hard, even more diligently than when I was at my own home. No matter how unpleasant my mother-in-law's expression was or how harsh my husband's words were, I endured it all silently. I was afraid they wouldn't be happy, afraid that even this family wouldn't want me anymore. I remember what my father told me before he died: "Xiao Shuang, be kind and tolerant as a person." I thought this way I could live peacefully. But because I couldn't get pregnant, everything changed. My husband, with whom I never registered our marriage, didn't even come home anymore. I felt wronged but didn't even dare to cry out loud. I could only secretly shed tears under my blanket at night, afraid they would hear and despise me even more. Later, my brother-in-law was getting married, and my mother-in-law told me to move out to make room for the newlyweds. I was so scared I trembled all over, and quietly said to her, "Mom, I have nowhere to go, please don't drive me away." My mother-in-law glared at me and said there were plenty of empty houses next door, and they couldn't possibly make the new bride suffer. At that moment, her look reminded me of those children who bullied me when I was young. I was really scared. Later, having nowhere to live, I moved into the old house in the attic. But even so, they still came looking for me, saying that after all these years of eating and living at their expense, I must give them living expenses. If I didn't, they would come every day and make it impossible for me to hold my head up in the village. I was afraid they would really make a scene. I have no father, no mother, no one to stand up for me. I'm very obedient and don't know what else to do. Every time they took the money away, my heart felt like it was being cut. That was my hard-earned money saved penny by penny from washing dishes and moving goods. Until I met Brother Dacheng, he was like a lamp in the darkness. For the first time, he made me believe there are people in this world who give without expecting anything in return. It was his casual kindness that helped me when I was about to fall. I'm even more grateful to my father for teaching me with his simple life that people can be poor, but cannot lose their kind heart. This lesson is the consolation for all the bitter days I've lived through. Now I finally understand that a real home is not something you beg for or settle for, but the moment when two sincere hearts illuminate each other. I also thank the uncles and aunties in front of the screen for your support and companionship along the way, which gave me the courage to build a home that truly belongs to me.; actions: type: watch, play_duration: 6, played_loop_cnt: 0, is_complete_play: False, is_fast_forward_play: False, is_backward_play: False, is_enlarge_play: False

Every time the mother finished feeding her daughter instant noodles, she would carefully save the leftover soup. Then, when no one was around, she would quietly walk to the hospital stairwell, take out a dried and hardened steamed bun from her pocket, dip it in her daughter's leftover soup, and stuff it into her mouth bite by bite. This scene happened to be witnessed by a passing little boy. Unable to bear it, the boy gave her his birthday cake: "Grandma, don't eat the bun anymore. Eat mine instead. This is really delicious." Unexpectedly, the moment the woman saw the boy, her emotions became inexplicably agitated, simply because the boy looked too much like her son Yanwen from 20 years ago. She couldn't help but reach out to touch the boy's face, forgetting that even if her son were still alive, he shouldn't be this age. The boy's father, thinking the woman meant harm to his son, kicked her against the wall. But what he could never have imagined was that this strange woman before him was the biological mother he had been searching for over 20 years. It turned out that 20 years ago, he and his sister both had heart disease, and his condition was more severe—he only had 7 days left. But their mother, who relied on farming for a living, simply couldn't afford the expensive surgery fees. When she was at her wit's end, a neighbor introduced a wealthy childless person. Only by giving her son to them could the child survive. What mother would be willing to give away her own flesh and blood? "Even if I have to sell everything, sell my blood, sell my kidney, I will save Yanwen and Linlin." But before she could finish speaking, her son's heart condition flared up and he lost consciousness. Without immediate treatment, he might not survive the night. To save her son's life, the mother could only tearfully carry him to the car, but fearing her stubborn son would secretly run back, she deliberately said some hurtful words: "You're just a burden. If I keep raising you, you'll drag down this whole family. I can no longer afford it. Leave now. I never want to see you, this deadweight, again." Little did she know this well-intentioned lie would make her son hate her for a full 20 years. Twenty years later, after becoming a company president, the son's first act was to return home with his wife and child, wanting to make that hateful mother kneel and apologize. However, the moment he opened the door, he found a strange man coming out. The president learned from him that to pay for his sister's treatment, his mother had sold the house to him 20 years ago, but his sister still died because there was no money for surgery. He pressed for his mother's whereabouts. The man replied: "She's probably dead too. Otherwise, how could she not have come back for over ten years?" Hearing that both his mother and sister had passed away, the president's heart suddenly contracted. Twenty years of love and hate collapsed completely in that moment. However, both mother and sister were actually still alive. Over these years, the woman in her sixties worked three jobs simultaneously every day, specifically choosing high-paying dirty and exhausting work, just to save up for surgery fees as soon as possible. However, when she heard that heart surgery required 200,000 yuan, she still collapsed on the ground in despair: "200,000! Where am I supposed to get that much money?" She could only lie about her age to apply for high-altitude work, as this was the fastest way to make money. Unexpectedly, on her first day, the safety rope malfunctioned, but fortunately she survived. Coincidentally, this company was under her son's business empire. After 20 years apart, mother and son met again, but they didn't recognize each other. The president only felt the woman before him was familiar. Having previously heard his mother had died, he didn't think much of it. To keep her job, the woman knelt before the president on the spot. Hearing she was trying to pay for her daughter's treatment, the president suddenly thought of his own mother. "If my mother had been half as responsible back then, perhaps I wouldn't be like this now." Out of shared tragic circumstances, the president had his wife give her 2,000 yuan directly. But this was still far from enough for surgery fees, so she pleaded with the president, hoping he would let her stay and continue working. Only then did the man feel endless regret, but it was already too late. It turned out the man was addicted to gambling. After draining all his wife's money, he still wasn't satisfied and even forced her to sell her blood. Unable to endure this hellish torment any longer, his wife left this world with their two children. From that moment on, the man turned over a new leaf. Twenty years passed in the blink of an eye, and the former gambling addict had become a renowned business tycoon. Yet he had been living with guilt over his wife and children, even dreaming every day of his wife personally poisoning herself and the children. This day, the man finally couldn't bear the inner torment. Just as he was about to jump off a building, time suddenly reversed. The man discovered in horror that he had returned to the day before his wife's death. Before he could react, his wife suddenly returned home with the two children. "Zhao Qinghan, when did you get back?" Seeing his wife and children alive before him, the man instantly became excited and wanted to give them a big hug. Unexpectedly, his son told him to get out and said he wasn't worthy of being his father. Seeing this, the man immediately knelt on the ground begging for their forgiveness, not only promising he would never gamble again, but also swearing to heaven he would give them a good life. But his wife's ears had heard these words so many times they had calluses, and she refused to believe him anymore. However, fearing he would become emotional and beat her and the children again, she took out the few yuan she had just gotten from selling her blood. But after taking the money, the man didn't think about gambling; instead, he wanted to buy some food to bring back. Unexpectedly, as soon as he went out, the neighbors all avoided him, because in his previous life the man was addicted to gambling, and no one was willing to give him a kind look. The man felt very dejected and immediately vowed he would definitely make big money and give his wife and children a good life. Looking at the crumpled few yuan in his hand, the man couldn't think of a good way to make money for a moment. He suddenly saw a handsome guy on a motorcycle at the intersection—it was his childhood friend who had gotten rich selling soap in his previous life.
